originality.rationale: The six-cycle \(n=3\) values are explicitly known by Gu and the \(n=4\) cube case is implied by the Cartesian-product Künneth theorem. New is the uniform vanishing for every \(n\geq5\) in two off-diagonal integral groups even though these crowns contain isometric six-cycles. Beyond the already known six-cycle and cube cases, primary theorems on cycles, pawful graphs, Cartesian-product Kunneth and girth do not cover \(n\geq5\) crown metric chains; searched related published calculations address different graphs. Unindexed stronger/equivalent sources remain a risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent crown-graph calculation or stronger theorem may not have appeared in the bounded searches.
The finite numerical checks do not exclude higher-degree off-diagonal groups and are not used to establish global diagonality.

value.rationale: For every \(n\geq5\) the canonical crown graph contains isometric C6 copies with known nonzero magnitude homology, yet both first low off-diagonal integral groups of the ambient graph vanish; the boundary \(n=4\) is already known from cube diagonality. The sharp \(n=3\) to \(n\geq4\) transition for a natural infinite graph family yields structural information about noninjectivity under metric embeddings and a concrete test case for general diagonality methods. It goes beyond a narrow accidental computation.
